title: Why Cats Bring Home Dead Prey
topic: Why do cats bring you dead animals?

lines: Ever wonder why your cat drags a dead mouse to your doorstep?

beats.text: Cats are obligate predators. Even well‑fed house cats still stalk and pounce.
lines: Cats are obligate predators. Even well‑fed house cats still stalk and pounce.
Hunting satisfies a built‑in nutritional need and lets them practice skills needed in the wild.
A single mouse provides the right temperature and protein balance cats instinctively seek.

beats.text: The behavior is mostly instinctual; kittens play‑hunt long before they ever see a human hand.
lines: The behavior is mostly instinctual; kittens play‑hunt long before they ever see a human hand.

beats.title: Indoor vs Outdoor

verdict.text: Breed matters little; all felines share the same hunting circuitry.

lines: Outdoor access and early life experiences increase kills, while neutered or indoor cats show fewer gifts.
Breed matters little; all felines share the same hunting circuitry.
Try a feather wand or puzzle feeder so your cat can hunt safely at home.

sources.claim: Cats hunt small prey such as birds and rodents.
Hunting behavior is driven by evolutionary constraints and nutritional requirements.
Play mimics hunting and helps kittens learn stalking and killing skills.
Environment, outdoor access, and early life history influence how often cats kill prey; breed is not a major factor.
